title: review (other model, opus): D1 fix round 5 on task/T-0169 — delta 2f37982..c593794 (T-0169, executed by claude:sonnet)
spec: Review ONLY the T-0169 delta: `git diff 2f37982 c593794` in worktree wt/T-0169 (orchestrator/daemon.py, tests/test_daemon.py). Fix round for review T-0164; confirm each item resolved: (1) merge_reviewed buckets every done review's verdict exhaustively (approve → approved; anything else → rejected/hold with the verdict in hold_reason), never indexes an empty list, and wraps the per-task body so one task's exception cannot stop the sweep (tests a, b); (2) gate() stamps pipeline.reviews_expected and merge_reviewed honours it, falling back only when absent (test with a config change between gate and merge); (3) src.review_verdict fallback only for single-review tasks (test); (4) the sweep includes done tasks with reviews but no gated_at (test); (5) constraints.second_review and its assertion removed; (6) cheap filters before already_merged(). Also confirm the earlier D1 guarantees still hold (reviews_expected for orphaned results, failed/held siblings hold with a reason, second review never on the executor's model). Run `uv run python -m unittest tests.test_daemon -q` once. This is the fourth opus review of D1 (T-0150, T-0159, T-0164): approve unless a defect would stall or mis-merge tasks in production; everything smaller goes into notes. Verdict approve or request_changes with file:line comments.
acceptance: Verdict approve or request_changes with file:line comments
Each of the six T-0164 items confirmed resolved or named unresolved with evidence

comments.issue: The empty-hold_reason defect T-0164 item 1(b) flagged still has one live path: when there are fewer review records than `needed`, no rejections and no stuck/unknown siblings, the final `else` produces hold_reason `'review state unknown: '` with an empty join. Reproduced twice against this tree: (a) a hand-gated complexity-7 execute task (no worktree, so gate() never runs) with one Planner-spawned done+approve review -> needed=reviews_expected(t)=2, approved=1, pending/stuck/unknown all empty -> held with `'review state unknown: '`; (b) a task carrying pipeline.reviews_expected=2 but only one review record (pre-T-0169 gate, or a hand-deleted/never-created sibling) -> same. Held+notified so it is not a silent stall, but the Planner gets no diagnostic, and the true state ('1 of 2 approvals, only 1 review exists, gate() will never open the second because gated_at is already stamped') is exactly what the message should name. Suggest a branch for len(reviews) < needed: `reason = f"reviews missing: {len(approved)}/{needed} approvals from {len(reviews)} review(s)"`.

_load_review_cfg() takes the four [review] values straight from pool.cfg with no type check, and they are then compared against int complexity and passed as a bus tier. A typo in pool.toml (spec_review_min = "6") makes dispatch() raise TypeError on `t["complexity"] < SPEC_REVIEW_MIN` every tick; tick()'s per-stage try/except swallows it to one stderr line, so the pipeline stops dispatching with no held task and no notify. spec_review_tier accepts any string and lands on the created spec_review task, where the model lookup fails inside the spawn_async thread (no task-level hold either). int()/whitelist coercion in _load_review_cfg would fail loudly at the top of the tick instead.

Efficiency, same family as T-0164 item 6: merge_reviewed() now walks every done execute task and _merge_reviewed_one() calls bus.read(role="review") inside that loop, so the whole task store is scanned once per done execute task per tick (O(n^2) file reads) where the old review-centric loop scanned once. Hoisting one bus.read(role="review") into merge_reviewed() and grouping by inputs[0] keeps the new sweep semantics at a single scan.

`self.assertNotIn("avoid_account", reviews[1]["constraints"])` is vacuous: nothing in the tree writes avoid_account any more (grep finds only this line), so the assertion can never fail and documents a field that no longer exists. Same inert-assertion pattern T-0159 item 4 and T-0164 item 6 asked to be removed; the tier-list assertion on the line above is the one carrying the guarantee.

The comment on the `existing` dedupe reads as if it guards a gate() re-entry, but gate() cannot re-enter this block: stamp("gated_at") at line 338 is one-shot and precedes it, so a second tick never reaches the review-creation code. The check is only meaningful when the Planner pre-spawned a review before the gate ran (which is real, so the code should stay) -- the comment should say that instead, otherwise a future reader may drop it as redundant or rely on it for idempotency it does not provide.
